# Source Code

#### Course: Learn Recursion With Java

## Source Code

```java
1class Main {
2
3    public static int fib(int n) {
4
5        // Base Case
6        // If number is 1 or 0, return it
7        if (n == 1 || n == 0) {
8            return n;
9        }
10        
11        // Return sum of previous two Fibonacci numbers
12        return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
13    }
14
15    public static void main(String[] args) {
16
17        int result = fib(4);
18        System.out.println(result);
19    }
20}
```

Output

```text
3
```

For the sake of simplicity, we are only printing the value at the n index of the series i.e. the number at the (n + 1)th position.

Since n == 4, the above output gives the value of the Fibonacci series at the fifth position.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

By the way, here's the equivalent code using an object instead of a static method.

```java
1class Main {
2
3    public static int fib(int n) {
4
5        if (n == 1 || n == 0) {
6            return n;
7        }
8        
9        return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
10    }
11
12    public static void main(String[] args) {
13
14        Main obj = new Main();
15
16        int result = obj.fib(4);
17        System.out.println(result);
18    }
19}
```
